ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 7 — Focused Visit (Care-plan review) — Frederick Cook

code.originalText: Sixteen-week review: blood pressure, potassium and kidney function on losartan, mood, social needs and stroke prevention

text.paragraph: Sixteen-week review of blood pressure, potassium and kidney function four weeks after starting losartan; mood and stroke prevention. [S]

Mr. Cook returns four weeks after changing from hydrochlorothiazide to losartan 50 mg, with amlodipine 5 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg and aspirin 81 mg. He has no dizziness, cough or swelling, and no gout. His home readings average 124/76. He did not have the blood test that was meant to be done one to two weeks after starting losartan; it was drawn this morning. His prison medical records have arrived and record no earlier diagnoses or vaccinations. His fecal immunochemical test was negative. He feels more settled, is writing every morning, and still feels a sting of shame when he is recognized, though it troubles him less. He has had no stroke symptoms. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-10-27; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well; blood pressure 126/76, pulse 66, weight 74.8 kg

Elevated blood pressure at the first visit, 166/94 mmHg (average of two seated readings), without a previous diagnosis of hypertension; no symptoms; out-of-office confirmation with a week of home readings requested
S — Synthetic presenting finding at re-entry; superseded by the diagnosis at the second visit.
Essential hypertension, stage 2, confirmed by home readings averaging 154/90 mmHg; no left ventricular hypertrophy on ECG; urine albumin normal
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis made at the second visit.
Right carotid bruit heard at the first visit in a man with no symptoms of stroke or transient ischemic attack; carotid duplex ultrasound and vascular neurology consultation requested
S — Synthetic examination finding; superseded by the duplex result at the second visit.

Asymptomatic atherosclerotic stenosis of the right internal carotid artery, 50 to 69 percent by duplex ultrasound, with less than 50 percent plaque on the left; no stroke or transient ischemic attack; managed with best medical therapy (blood pressure control, a statin and low-dose aspirin) and yearly duplex surveillance
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis made at the vascular neurology consultation; not a claim about his real arteries.

Recent release from about six years of incarceration: re-entering community life on parole at 65, establishing primary care with no medical records yet received, a rented room, no earned income, and a public reputation he feels as a burden
S — Synthetic modern social problem anchored to his documented imprisonment and parole.

Acute gout of the right first metatarsophalangeal joint, a first flare seven weeks after starting hydrochlorothiazide, diagnosed clinically (sudden overnight onset, redness, swelling and exquisite tenderness of the big toe, no fever); treated with low-dose colchicine; resolved
S — Synthetic adverse drug effect; not a historical claim.
